abstracts.value: Quantum gravity is expected to play a central role in resolving classical singularities and providing a complete, predictive spacetime picture. In this paper, we develop an effective model inspired by loop quantum gravity that aims to fulfill this expectation, providing a unified description of thin shell collapse, black hole formation, evaporation, and remnant dynamics. The framework exhibits general validity, holding across different effective equations of motion, matter sources, and evaporation laws. Specifically, we incorporate backreaction within a quasi-static approximation, modeling the radiation as null dust and matching the ingoing and outgoing fluxes across an evaporation surface using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. For an evaporation law governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, we find that the final stage of evaporation yields an extremal black hole extending into a new asymptotic region, featuring both event and Cauchy horizons. Conversely, under the Schwinger approach, no event or Cauchy horizons form, instead, a temporary dynamical trapped region emerges, and the resulting spacetime remains globally hyperbolic. Under this variant, our model predicts a horizonless null remnant escaping to future null infinity.

titles.title: Quantum black hole evaporation from thin shell collapse: a complete effective picture

abstracts.value: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding the singularity problem. Based on backward ray tracing method, this work investigates both the optical and polarimetric observational features of rotating Ayón-Beato-García spacetime with regularization parameter $Q$. It is found that, compared with the Kerr case, the parameter $Q$ leads to a significant contraction of the size of the inner shadow in the observed optical images. This contraction remains visible even after an illustrative Gaussian filter for images observed at a low inclination angle (e.g. $17^\circ$). In the polarized images, we focus on two observables, the electric vector position angles (EVPAs) and the depolarization regions, on the observer's screen. It is found that depolarization regions do not necessarily reside in the vicinity of the bright photon ring in images at high inclination angles (e.g. $83^\circ$), and a multi-branch structure can be observed. Furthermore, the distribution of EVPAs is insensitive to the regularization parameter $Q$ while the morphology of the depolarization regions can be impacted remarkably by $Q$. The results provide possible optical observable characteristics for the rotating regular spacetime.

titles.title: Probing the Macroscopic Imprints of Singularity Resolution: Polarization Diagnostics of Rotating ABG Black Holes

abstracts.value: Identical critical curves need not imply identical null-orbit dynamics. For a class of static spherical areal-radius deformations, we show that a surviving original photon sphere retains its critical impact parameter and orbital frequency, while its coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent is multiplied by the radial Jacobian. The logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient acquires the inverse factor. At a reflection-symmetric throat, stability factorizes into a derivative of the original optical potential and the throat curvature. More generally, an order-$m$ extremum of the original potential composed with an order-$q$ areal-radius minimum produces an optical degeneracy of order $p=mq$, with critical approach $|x|\propto|t|^{-2/(p-2)}$ and reflected strong deflection $Δϕ\propto(b/b_{\rm c}-1)^{-(p-2)/(2p)}$ for $p>2$. For the Simpson--Visser family with mass $M$ and bounce parameter $a$, the critical impact parameter remains Schwarzschild-like for $a<3M$, although the instability varies with $a$. The merger at $a=3M$ is quartic, separating stable and unstable throat branches. These results isolate the null-orbit information preserved by a radial deformation from that encoded in its local geometry.

titles.title: Critical curves and throat degeneracy in black bounces

abstracts.value: We present new black hole solutions for the class of gravitational effective field theories in four spacetime dimensions that extend General Relativity while retaining the graviton as the only degree of freedom of gravitational origin. We consider terms up to cubic order in curvature, solve the resulting field equations, and find one-way hidden wormholes as numerical solutions: these are regular black holes with an interior wormhole throat that is crossable in one direction and leads to a cosmological spacetime in its interior. They are regular and have no inner horizon, thus evading the mass inflation instability that afflicts conventional regular black hole geometries.

titles.title: Hidden wormholes from an action principle in $D=4$

abstracts.value: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.

titles.title: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk

abstracts.value: It remains unclear which gravitational-wave channel constrains which feature of a black-hole deformation. We address this for a new two-parameter family of static black holes in which the leading inverse-cube quantum correction to the Newtonian potential is resummed by a Padé approximant into a bounded mass function, <math altimg="si106.svg"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo linebreak="badbreak">+</mo><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></math>. The screening amplitude ϵ and length ℓ fix a cubic horizon equation, an effective source obeying the null and weak energy conditions for ϵ > 0, and a strictly positive axial perturbation potential. We compute the <math altimg="si4.svg"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si107.svg"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> quasinormal modes with a Chebyshev spectral solver, validated against Schwarzschild and time-domain evolutions, and evolve adiabatic extreme-mass-ratio inspirals with exact geodesic energetics. A Bayesian analysis of explicitly synthetic ringdown data shows that a third-generation event bounds the tail coefficient <math altimg="si108.svg"><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> to |κ| < 0.11 at 90% credibility and detects a benchmark deviation with <math altimg="si109.svg"><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mi mathvariant="script">B</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>6.86</mn></mrow></math>. A year-long inspiral into a 10<sup loc="post">6</sup> M⊙ black hole accumulates a dephasing |ΔΦ| ≈ 7.71 × 10<sup loc="post">4</sup> |κ| rad ( ≈ 20% flux-model uncertainty), giving sensitivity to <math altimg="si110.svg"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> when ℓ scales with mass; for fixed ℓ, stellar-mass ringdowns give the stronger bound. Because both channels depend predominantly on κ, combining them breaks the ϵ–ℓ degeneracy only weakly.

titles.title: Padé-screened quantum-corrected black holes: Ringdown spectroscopy and extreme-mass-ratio dephasing as complementary gravitational-wave probes

abstracts.value: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

titles.title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description

abstracts.value: We investigate the physical realization and observational properties of Damour--Solodukhin wormholes within general relativity. We first construct an explicit matter source supporting this geometry, consisting of a phantom scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, and examine both electric and magnetic configurations. We then study the propagation of photons and derive constraints on the wormhole deformation parameter $λ$ using Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*. We show that, for $λ^2 \leq 1/2$, the shadow radius coincides exactly with the Schwarzschild value, although the radial geometry continues to affect gravitational lensing and the structure of photon rings. Using a thin accretion disk with a Johnson SU emissivity profile, we investigate the resulting optical images and examine the effects of the wormhole throat on their structure. Finally, we analyze stationary relativistic accretion and demonstrate that, for identical boundary conditions, the energy density and particle number density are independent of $λ$ throughout the common exterior region, while the radial velocity retains an explicit dependence on the deformation parameter. We also derive the condition $0 < w < (1+4λ^2)^{-1}$ for the existence of an exterior sonic point. These results highlight the observational degeneracy between Damour--Solodukhin wormholes and Schwarzschild black holes in the small-deformation regime, while identifying the geometric and dynamical effects through which this degeneracy may be investigated.

titles.title: Damour--Solodukhin Wormholes: Matter Sources, Observational Constraints, and Accretion Dynamics

abstracts.value: We study critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters in stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with separable null geodesics and Kerr angular structure. A Kerr-relative decomposition of the radial metric functions gives analytic first-order departures of these observables for observers at general inclination. The critical curve's signed normal displacement factorizes as $\tilde u_n=\tilde F_{\mathrm K}\mathscr C$, where $\tilde F_{\mathrm K}$ depends only on the Kerr reference geometry and $\mathscr C$ is an explicit combination of optical metric deviations. The demagnification exponent, time delay, and azimuthal advance are evaluated at a common position angle on the observer screen. Intrinsic relations among the exact observables express the optical information shared by the curve, time delay, and azimuthal advance, while demagnification additionally depends on radial instability. Applications to representative metrics illustrate how different radial deformations produce distinct departures from Kerr around the critical curve. Comparisons with exact finite-deformation profiles and independent numerical calculations verify the first-order predictions on regular, accessible exterior photon-shell branches.

titles.title: Deviations from Kerr: Critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters for general observer inclinations

abstracts.value: We investigate the interplay between physics beyond the Standard Model and modified spacetime geometries in shaping the photon and neutrino spectra from evaporating black holes. We implement three representative supersymmetric (SuSy) benchmarks and a composite dynamics (CoDy) scenario in BlackHawk. We consider both Schwarzschild black holes and regular black holes geometries, namely polymerized, Hayward, and Simpson--Visser black holes. New degrees of freedom at the TeV scale become accessible at Hawking temperatures corresponding to black hole masses of approximately $M_{\rm BH}\sim 10^{10}\,\mathrm{g}$. We show that physics beyond the Standard Model produces distinctive signatures in both the instantaneous secondary-photon and neutrino spectra. Radiative decays generate narrow spectral features with approximately temperature-independent relative amplitudes, while multistep decay cascades produce broad enhancements that become increasingly pronounced at higher temperatures. In contrast, compressed mass spectra exhibit no localized features. Crucially, we show that the effects of new particle physics and modified spacetime geometries can become intertwined in specific energy regimes, altering the resulting spectral signatures. Our results demonstrate that photon and neutrino spectra provide complementary probes of new particle physics and black hole geometry, with predicted spectral enhancements extending into the energy ranges accessible to current and future high-energy observatories.

titles.title: SuSy and CoDy Radiation from Evaporating Black Holes

abstracts.value: We study the linear stability of Simpson-Visser ``black-bounce'' space-times (regular black holes and wormholes) under spherically symmetric (monopole) perturbations, taking as a source a phantom scalar field with a self-interaction potential and a magnetic field within nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). The metric contains two parameters: the mass $M$ and the bounce parameter $a >0$, such that $a \leq 2M$ corresponds to black holes and $a > 2M$ to wormholes. The stability problem reduces to a boundary-value problem for a Schrödinger-like equation with a certain effective potential. All space-times under study are found to be unstable, and the corresponding exponential growth rates are calculated. For black holes the results are obtained without complications, while the wormhole stability problem faces difficulties that seem to be previously unnoticed. Thus, the Darboux transformation, used to remove the wall shaped $\approx 2/z^2$ in the effective potentials at wormhole throats ($z$ is the tortoise coordinate), creates nonphysical poles outside the throat for $a/(2M) \lesssim 4.98$. We circumvent this difficulty by using a gauge-invariant approach in the spirit of Cremona, Pizzocchero and Sarbach, leading to a master equation with a simple and regular potential. Its further analysis reveals unstable modes: the mode with a variable throat radius is always present; for $a/(2M) \gtrsim 4.98$ there are two real growing throat modes, which merge into a complex-conjugate pair (oscillatory instability) for smaller $a$. A further analysis reveals three exceptional points that separate ranges of $a/(2M)$ with different perturbation regimes. Furthermore, the leading unstable black-hole and wormhole modes approach the same limiting growth rate $Mκ\simeq 0.10121$ as $a/(2M)$ approaches unity from either side.

titles.title: Instabilities of Simpson-Visser black bounces sourced by a phantom scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics

abstracts.value: Regularizing a black hole removes its singularity, but which observations could detect the regularized core? We address this question for a Simpson-Visser black bounce built on the power-law hairy black hole that a Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond background produces. Measured in the areal radius, the bounce leaves the metric function untouched and changes only the radial measure. This single fact sorts the observables into two classes. The shadow, the innermost stable orbit, orbital frequencies and gravitational redshifts are blind to the throat. The instability of the photon ring, the brightness of its subrings, the oscillation phase of neutrinos and the energy deposited by neutrino pair annihilation respond to it through one universal factor. We derive an exact law for the subring demagnification that holds for any metric function. We also show that the throat enters the weak-field neutrino phase and the light deflection with different weights, so that combined photon and neutrino lensing can separate the mass from the throat. Ray-traced polarized images of a turbulent thin disk confirm that the direct image hides the throat while the first subring reveals it. For neutrinos emitted near a stellar-mass compact object the throat reshapes the flavor survival pattern and enhances the annihilation energy deposition. Two independent computations reproduce each headline number.

titles.title: Kalb-Ramond black bounces: throat-blind shadows and throat-sensitive neutrinos

abstracts.value: We study steady, spherically symmetric accretion of a collisionless kinetic gas onto a compact object described by the Simpson--Visser (SV) metric, a one-parameter regularization of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Using the standard relativistic Vlasov formalism, we adopt boundary conditions at a finite injection radius $R$ and compute the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$ for Vlasov gas with both monoenergetic and Maxwell--Jüttner distribution functions. Throughout the computation, we also take into account the influence of particle's angular momentum. We carefully investigate the influence of the black bounce parameter on the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$. By expanding accretion rate in terms of bounce parameter $a$, we found that the leading-order correction appears at quadratic order in $a$. This work extends the Vlasov accretion framework to a broader class of spherically symmetric spacetimes and quantifies the impact of the geometric modification on the accretion flow. In particular, since the shadows of the SV and Schwarzschild black holes are degenerate, comparing their mass accretion rates may offer a complementary probe for distinguishing these geometries in future astrophysical observations.

titles.title: Probing black bounce spacetime through mass accretion rate

abstracts.value: The inner horizon of stationary black holes is subject to classical and semiclassical instabilities, suggesting that the Kerr interior should be modified. Quantum backreaction may drive the curvature to the Planck scale, producing a spacelike singularity, or halt its growth at lower curvatures, leading to a regular black bounce. We investigate the phenomenology of these two possibilities using, respectively, a Gürses--Gürsey geometry with a spacelike singularity and the rotating Simpson--Visser black bounce. Both geometries reproduce the light ring and ISCO frequencies of a Kerr black hole with the same ADM mass and angular momentum, by calibration in the first case and identically in the second. We find that the null and timelike convergence conditions are violated outside the horizon, up to a finite radius beyond the light ring in the Gürses--Gürsey geometry and everywhere in the rotating Simpson--Visser spacetime. Moreover, their fundamental scalar quasinormal modes deviate from those of Kerr, most markedly in the damping, which is enhanced in the Gürses--Gürsey geometry and reduced in the rotating Simpson--Visser one. Thus, agreement with Kerr in a limited set of observables is not sufficient to establish the Kerr nature of a compact object, motivating complementary observational tests.

titles.title: Testing the Kerr hypothesis with orbital frequencies: lessons from spacelike singularities and black bounces

abstracts.value: Using the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism, we study energy extraction from the Teo traversable rotating wormhole at different orbital locations. This wormhole has no event horizon and cannot reduce to a Kerr black hole in any parameter limit. We compute circular orbits on the equatorial plane, the prograde photon sphere, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We find that below a certain spin, no circular orbit exists inside the ergosphere. Both the efficiency and power calculated from magnetic reconnection increase monotonically with angular momentum. Compared with a Kerr black hole under the same plasma parameters, the Teo wormhole has higher energy extraction power and efficiency. This is completely different from the Simpson-Visser rotating wormhole, which can reduce to a Kerr black hole, where the large spin makes efficiency and power decrease. We also extend magnetic reconnection to the plunging region. We find that when the spin is not particularly high, the energy extraction power and efficiency in the plunging region are higher than those in the circular orbit region, while for very high spin the situation is reversed. This conclusion also differs from that obtained from a Kerr black hole, where the power and efficiency in the plunging region are always higher than those in the circular orbit region.

We find that below a certain spin, no circular orbit exists inside the ergosphere. Both the efficiency and power calculated from magnetic reconnection increase monotonically with angular momentum. titles.title: Extracting energy from a traversable wormhole via magnetic reconnection: Circular orbits and the plunging region
Extracting Energy from a Traversable Wormhole via Magnetic Reconnection: Circular Orbits and the Plunging Region

abstracts.value: Spinning test particles provide a precision probe of strong-field gravity, yet their dynamics around singularity-free black holes in conformal gravity remain poorly constrained. We investigate equatorial motion around the non-singular Schwarzschild black hole of conformal gravity, in which the conformal scale \(L\) removes the curvature divergence at the origin while preserving the event horizon at \(r=2M\) and recovering the Schwarzschild geometry as \(L\to 0\). Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we derive the conserved energy and angular momentum in the conformally rescaled spherical spacetime and construct the radial effective potential for spinning particles. This allows us to determine the physical timelike spin bound, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), the degeneracy between \(L\) and the Kerr rotation parameter, and representative bound trajectories. We show that \(L\) strengthens the effective-potential barrier, decreases the ISCO radius, angular momentum and energy, and lowers the maximum admissible spin before the trajectory becomes spacelike. The orbital integrations reveal a clear division of roles: \(L\) governs the compactness of the bound orbit, whereas the particle spin governs the accumulated relativistic precession. These results establish spinning-particle dynamics as a sensitive diagnostic of conformally regular black-hole spacetimes and provide a possible route to distinguish the conformal Schwarzschild geometry from standard Schwarzschild background.

titles.title: Spinning particle dynamics around a non-singular Schwarzschild black hole in conformal gravity

abstracts.value: Regular black holes (RBHs) are often constructed with a regular point-like center and two horizons, including an inner Cauchy horizon susceptible to mass inflation. We show that a two-horizon structure is not a necessary consequence of regularity. For static, spherically symmetric geometries with an asymptotically static exterior, we establish a horizon-parity theorem: a regular point-like center requires an even number of sign-changing zeros of $f$. We then construct two classes of single-horizon RBHs with a finite-area core, distinguished by whether the horizon lies outside the core or coincides with it, and analyze their matter content, energy conditions, and thermodynamic properties. The absence of an inner Cauchy horizon eliminates the classical mass-inflation mechanism on the single-horizon patch. We further establish mode stability against scalar perturbations for these finite-area-core configurations by showing that the effective potential is non-negative. Our results establish how the central geometry and asymptotic structure constrain horizon multiplicity and identify single-horizon configurations that avoid the classical inner-horizon instability.

titles.title: Single-horizon regular black holes and the fate of the inner-horizon instability

abstracts.value: We discuss possibilities of finding exact regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with temporal and radial components of the bumblebee field. We consider quadratic and linear potentials, with vanishing and nonzero cosmological constants, respectively. The field equations determine the nonminimal coupling and the relations between the model parameters. Found solution produce regular planar black hole with planar deformation function. Analytical expressions for this functions has been found. This solutions free of singularities at the $r=0$.

titles.title: Exact Regular Planar Black Holes solutions in Bumblebee gravity

abstracts.value: In this manuscript, we study circular geodesics and twin-peak high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillations (HF-QPOs) in the charged Simpson--Visser--anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime, which depends on a charge parameter $Q$, a regularization scale $b$ and an AdS radius $l$. Written in terms of the areal radius $R=\sqrt{r^{2}+b^{2}}$, the specific energy, angular momentum, Keplerian frequency and innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) of test particles coincide with those of the Reissner--Nordström--AdS black hole, so $b$ enters the epicyclic spectrum only through a factor $1-b^{2}/R^{2}$ in the radial frequency. We give this frequency and the ISCO condition in closed form. We then fit the relativistic-precession model to the HF-QPO pairs of GRO~J1655$-$40 and XTE~J1550$-$564, with their dynamical masses included as Gaussian priors. The Schwarzschild limit gives $χ^{2}=32.9$ for two degrees of freedom. One additional deformation removes this tension: $Q/M=0.814^{+0.059}_{-0.074}$ at fixed $l=100M$, or $l=40.6^{+6.2}_{-4.8}\,M$ at $Q=0$, both with $χ^{2}\simeq0.13$. These two solutions lie on a single degeneracy valley in the $(Q,l)$ plane, and, at $l=100M$, $b$ is left unconstrained up to $b\simeq3.9M$ (68%), a limit set by the charge prior rather than by the data. A Kerr black hole with spin $a\simeq0.3$--$0.4$ reproduces the same pairs, so the inferred deformation most likely absorbs the spin neglected by the static metric. Our results therefore describe degeneracies among orbital-frequency deformations; they are not a measurement of an electric charge or of a cosmological constant.

titles.title: Testing charged Simpson-Visser-AdS spacetimes with twin-peak QPOs

abstracts.value: The longstanding issue of whether horizonless compact objects can mimic black holes at horizon scales is addressed, a problem that persists because the shadow diameter alone is degenerate across a wide class of geometries. For slowly rotating traversable wormholes, we precisely formulate the optical appearance as a set of observables derived from equatorial null geodesics, yielding necessary and sufficient conditions for a multi-parameter fingerprint. Using a new lapse function that interpolates between exponential and rational redshift profiles, we obtain the photon-sphere condition, the strong-deflection lensing coefficients, and the Lyapunov exponent in closed form. The equations yield two families of wormhole solutions dependent on logarithmic and exponential entropy parameters. We compare the resulting quantum-modified spacetimes with Kerr and four regular black holes. The shadow diameter is shown to be tunable to within $5\%$ to $11\%$ of Kerr for all models considered, so that $|R_{\rm sh}^{\rm WH}/R_{\rm sh}^{\rm Kerr}-1| \lesssim 0.11$ and the shadow alone cannot separate the models. The degeneracy is lifted when the rotational asymmetry, lensing coefficients, Lyapunov exponent, and orbital frequency are combined: for the $5$-component fingerprint $\mathbf{F}=(\Arot,\abar,\bbar, \Lya,\Oph)$, the fractional deviation $Δ_i=(F_i^{\rm WH}-F_i^{\rm Kerr})/ F_i^{\rm Kerr}$ satisfies $|Δ_i|\gtrsim 0.05$ for every component, with the largest departures in the second lensing coefficient and the Lyapunov exponent. The combined discrimination signal reaches a signal-to-noise ratio of about $3.8$ to $3.9$ against Kerr and about $3.7$ against the Kazakov--Solodukhin benchmark, which is sufficient to break the shadow-diameter degeneracy at the $10\%$ measurement level.

titles.title: Optical constraints on rotating logarithmic- and exponential-entropy wormholes from strong-field lensing

abstracts.value: We construct an exact Simpson-Visser solution in metric bumblebee gravity, supported by a phantom scalar, magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics, and a spacelike configuration of fixed norm. The independent vector equation determines a local Lagrange multiplier and a temporal component that permits a regular ingoing extension across metric horizons. Reconstruction of the matter functions identifies a continuous family of wormholes, null minimum geometries, and black-bounces within one action. In the black hole case, the areal photon sphere and critical timelike orbit radii retain their Schwarzschild values, whereas angular deflection, periapsis advance, and photon orbit instability depend on the bounce and bumblebee parameters. The metric shadow coincides with the Schwarzschild prediction at fixed lapse mass and areal observer position; in addition, the adopted Sgr A* shadow diameter and M87* angular mass comparisons do not determine these parameters separately. The coupled axial equations yield distinct tensor, metric, and transverse bumblebee characteristics. We compute fundamental auxiliary massless scalar and ordinary Maxwell probe resonances by Chebyshev spectral collocation and estimate the tensor and bumblebee resonance scales at leading geometric optics order. Nonnegative probe potentials exclude exponentially growing probe modes. For negative nonminimal coupling and a nonzero temporal case, however, the supporting electromagnetic field develops an angular gradient instability in its extraordinary polarization. The unstable characteristic persists in the coupled principal symbol, while a variational construction establishes growing modes on the fixed geometry and lower bounds on their growth rates.

titles.title: An exact Simpson-Visser family in bumblebee gravity

abstracts.value: We regularize the central density cusp of the Joshi--Malafarina--Narayan spacetime using a normalized kernel motivated by a zero-point length. For an unbounded cusp, the convolution and enclosed mass are obtained analytically; truncating this density gives a regular, horizonless tangential-pressure interior matched to Schwarzschild. Convolving the finite cloud instead preserves its total mass and yields a smooth matter tail. A compactness bound establishes horizon avoidance for this second prescription. We determine the central lapse, establish causal geodesic completeness despite extreme optical delays, derive a uniform optical-delay formula across the critical compactness, and identify the stable interior light ring of ultracompact configurations. The massless scalar probe operator is nonnegative, while semiclassical trapped modes exhibit strongly suppressed leakage. An explicit pressure-closure comparison separates robust geometric properties from closure-dependent delay exponents. Planck-scale examples illustrate extreme redshifts and delays, but their photon interpretation requires physics beyond classical propagation in the core. The construction specifies an effective static source, rather than a microscopic matter theory or a dynamical resolution of collapse.

titles.title: Dressing a naked singularity with zero-point length

abstracts.value: In this work, we investigate the thermal, dynamical, and optical properties of regular black holes immersed in two physically motivated dark matter environments, namely the Dehnen and Einasto dark matter halos. For both halo models, we analyze the influence of the dark matter parameters on the spacetime geometry and demonstrate that the resulting black hole solutions remain free from curvature singularities, as confirmed by the finiteness of the Ricci and Kretschmann scalars. The dynamical behavior of the system is explored through the evolution of massless scalar perturbations, where the effective potential and time-domain profiles reveal stable damped oscillations for all considered parameter values. Furthermore, we derive and examine the lower bound on the transmission coefficient to understand the impact of the surrounding dark matter on Hawking radiation transmission. Our results show that the halo parameters significantly modify the potential barrier, leading to noticeable changes in the propagation and escape probability of scalar waves. The optical characteristics are investigated within the framework of static spherical accretion, where the observed intensity, shadow radius, and photon-ring structure are computed. We find that the Dehnen halo generally reduces the shadow size and contracts the photon rings with increasing halo parameters, whereas the Einasto halo enlarges the shadow and enhances the lensing features as the scale parameter increases.

titles.title: Effects of different dark models onto the thermal and optical aspects of regular black holes

abstracts.value: We investigate the conditions under which black hole fragmentation, the splitting of a black hole into two or multiple smaller ones, may occur via an unspecified dynamics, which would have the topology of a pair-of-pants. We employ kinematical and entropical consideration on time-sliced quasistatic black hole configurations to check under what conditions the pants dynamics is permitted. In classical general relativity, the Bekenstein-Hawking area law forbids such processes for Schwarzschild black holes. For spinning Kerr black holes, purely kinematic analyses impose constraints that prevent fragmentation, even in regimes where entropy considerations might allow it, except possibly in near-extremal cases. We then hunt for scenarios where black holes can wear pants: from the well-known Gregory-Laflamme instability in higher dimensions, to the potential effect of superradiant instabilities in nonaxisymmetric radiation trapping, to finally gravitational models that modify the relations between entropy and/or horizon radius and the black hole mass in four dimensions. In all such cases, emission of small fragments can be entropically favored. However, its occurrence still depends on the kinematic configuration of the initial state. Our analysis clarifies the theoretical landscape where black holes may fragment, which is particularly relevant for primordial black holes and catastrophic events such as black hole mergers.

titles.title: When black holes admit pair-of-pants topologies

abstracts.value: We point out that for black holes (BH) of the same mass, despite of arising from two entirely different physical arguments, the peak frequency of the coarse-grained gravitational wave (GW) spectrum of gravitons $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}$ is very close to the peak frequency of the GW spectrum produced from binary BH mergers $f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}$. In particular, we find that $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}/f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}\approx 2.3$ independent from BH mass or population. If BHs are still evaporating, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{-1}$ with $M_i$ is the initial BH mass. If BHs evaporated in the radiation (matter) dominated era, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{1/2}$ ($\propto M_i$) respectively after taking into account redshift effect. Any deviation from the aforementioned magical ratio would indicate new BH physics. The sweetest frequency ballpark to look for this correlation is around $10^{14}\ \rm Hz-10^{20}\ \rm Hz$ where both GW spectra are allowed to have maximum amplitude. As a demonstration of what the new physics could be, we consider a phenomenological self-similar regular BH model of Hayward featuring a single hair parameter. The observed ratio of peak frequencies can be used to directly infer the hair parameter, along with crucial properties of the novel BH solution such as Hawking temperature, horizon size, and innermost stable circular orbit. We also comment on the pros and cons of correlating frequencies among other GW sources such as formation, population fluctuation, and sudden transition of adiabatic perturbation.

titles.title: Correlation between gravitational wave frequencies as a signature of new black hole physics

abstracts.value: Modifications of gravity beyond (vacuum) General Relativity have a subtle impact on the physics around black holes. Describing these effects across different observables is, however, a priori strongly model dependent. While effective descriptions of the geometry allow to efficiently capture deviations from benchmark predictions, they sometimes lack a clear passage towards (effective) new physics. Inspired by linear response theory, in this work I therefore propose a formalism that allows to calculate leading corrections of observables relative to the Schwarzschild black hole anywhere in space-time (outside of the horizon): the order of corrections is fixed through an eigenvalue $\mathcal{E}$ of the Einstein tensor, which is identified with an external energy momentum tensor that generates the deformation of the geometry. In this ways, $\mathcal{E}$ can be linked to effective physics models. Focusing on spherically symmetric and static black holes, I illustrate the approach at the hand of a number of observables in the vicinity of the horizon, such as characteristic quantities of particles moving around the black hole (e.g. the black hole shadow or the radius of the innermost stable circular orbit) or the spectrum of scalar quasi-normal modes. Reversing the logic, I argue that the knowledge of such observables provides non-trivial constraints on $\mathcal{E}$, which in turn grant insights into the effective physics in the vicinity of the black hole.

titles.title: Linear Response to Black Hole Deformations

abstracts.value: We investigate non-stationary wormhole geometries in General Relativity embedded in evolving cosmological backgrounds. We employ a Simpson-Visser-like regularization of the temporal coordinate of the $(n+1)$-dimensional FLRW metric, together with a homogeneous Cuscuton field, to construct cosmological backgrounds in which the scale factor remains finite and non-zero at the would-be initial singularity. We then consider two specific dynamical wormhole geometries: the four-dimensional defect wormhole and the topologically charged Perry-Mann type wormhole. We show that the former can be supported by a canonical scalar field with vanishing potential, while the latter requires a mimetic matter sector to support its spatial structure, with the Cuscuton governing the cosmological evolution in both cases. We subsequently generalize the analysis to a separable non-stationary spacetime and derive a scaling condition that strongly constrains the admissible matter sources. In particular, for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics fields, this condition removes the functional freedom available in static reconstruction schemes. We show that, within this framework, regular, asymptotically flat wormhole geometries cannot be obtained while simultaneously satisfying the required smoothness and reflection symmetry conditions. Our results illustrate both the possibility of constructing specific non-stationary wormholes in regular cosmological backgrounds and the restrictions that arise when attempting to generalize such constructions to arbitrary spatial geometries.

titles.title: Non-Stationary Wormholes and Matter Source Reconstruction in General Relativity

abstracts.value: In this work, we present the Simpson-Visser black-bounce (SV-BB) spacetime with both electric and magnetic charges (the dyonic SV-BB) as an exact solution of general relativity coupled to Maxwell electrodynamics and an anisotropic fluid with vanishing radial pressure. We assume the anisotropic fluid represents an Einstein cluster, which consists of a dense system of particles moving in circular orbits that generate only tangential pressure and zero radial pressure. We show that the electromagnetic SV-BB metric, which provides a regular black hole spacetime, can be obtained as an exact solution to the Einstein field equations sourced by a combination of an Einstein cluster (which is responsible for providing the exotic matter required to keep a black-bounce throat open) and an electromagnetic field in the framework of Maxwell electrodynamics.

titles.title: Dyonic Simpson Visser black-bounce spacetime surrounded by an exotic Einstein cluster in general relativity

abstracts.value: The S301 star reaches a pericentre one tenth that of S2, opening a new regime for probing black-hole spin and departures from Schwarzschild. We develop a post-Newtonian secular Hamiltonian framework for bound geodesics in stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes and compute the maximum projected astrometric deviation over one orbit. At the expected GRAVITY+ precision, S301 can probe several nonrotating geometries and sizeable spin-induced deviations, while kilometre-baseline interferometry can probe much smaller departures, establishing S301 as a powerful test of the spacetime geometry of Sgr A*.

titles.title: Probing departures from Schwarzschild geometry with the S301 star and kilometre-baseline interferometry

abstracts.value: We study the spherical geometry from the Simpson-Visser prescription $r\to\sqrt{r^2+a^2}$ to the quantum Oppenheimer-Snyder-Datt (qOSD) black hole of loop quantum cosmology, whose lapse function $A=1-2M/R+αM^2/R^4$ carries the correction $α$. This family interpolates between the qOSD black hole ($a\to0$), the Simpson-Visser black bounce ($α\to0$), and Schwarzschild. The geometry is regular for every $a>0$, the Ricci scalar at the throat is blind to $α$ while the Kretschmann scalar is not, and the null energy condition is violated at the throat by $-1/(4πa^2)$. The $(α,a)$ plane splits into a two-horizon regular black hole, a single-horizon black hole with a hidden bounce, no Cauchy horizon, and a traversable wormhole; the middle region removes the mass-inflation channel of regular black holes without fine tuning. Because circular orbits are governed by the areal radius, photon sphere, shadow, ISCO and azimuthal epicyclic frequency depend on $α$ only, whereas the Lyapunov exponent and radial epicyclic frequency carry the factor $\sqrt{1-a^2/R^2}$: shadow constrains only $α$, while ringdown damping and the twin-peak quasiperiodic-oscillation ratio are sensitive to $a$. We derive horizon thermodynamics with a first-law entropy that departs from the area law, show that the bounce changes the thermodynamic topological charge from $W=-1$ to $W=0$ at every $α$, and compute scalar, electromagnetic and Dirac quasinormal spectra using third-order WKB, Chebyshev spectral collocation and time-domain integration, which agree with one another and with eikonal scaling. Greybody bounds, Hawking emission, cascade sparsity and ringdown quality factor complete the analysis, and in the wormhole region the double-peaked potential produces echoes.

titles.title: Simpson-Visser regularization of the quantum Oppenheimer-Snyder-Datt black hole

abstracts.value: We argue that the local violation of null energy condition at the throat of a traversable wormhole does not necessarily indicate that the total volume integrated null energy contribution is negative. It is already known that it can be arbitrarily close to zero. We show that it can even be positive and use this argument to reconstruct a family of wormhole geometries. We also propose a novel classification of traversable wormholes based on the global volume integrated measure of null energy condition.

titles.title: Global Integrated Null Energy Contribution : Classification of Traversable Wormholes

abstracts.value: A basic question in the study of regular black holes is whether the Schwarzschild singularity can be replaced by a geodesically complete interior while retaining a single horizon. An asymptotic throat offers a minimal geometric realization of this possibility. The areal radius approaches a finite, nonzero limit at a future internal infinity, without requiring a change in spatial topology or a bounce. We extend the geometric analysis beyond monotone contraction to interiors in which the areal radius oscillates about its limit. For both null-type and spacelike-type inner ends, we derive a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for causal geodesic completeness and criteria for bounded curvature in parallel-propagated frames. Explicit examples of both types have complete inner ends and satisfy all four standard energy conditions at sufficiently large exterior radii. Applying these criteria to the oscillatory solution of the Böhmer--Vandersloot model of effective loop quantum gravity, we find a causally complete spacelike-type inner end. Its scalar curvature invariants converge to those of the limiting Nariai-type solution. Along each radial null geodesic, however, a parallel-propagated curvature component is unbounded along a sequence of turning points as the affine parameter tends to infinity.

titles.title: Asymptotic Throat as a Minimal Geometric Alternative to the Singularity in Schwarzschild Black Hole
Black Holes With Complete Asymptotic Throats

abstracts.value: Regular black holes (RBHs) and horizonless black hole mimickers (BHMs) are often studied as stationary alternatives to classical black holes, although their interiors may be unstable or undergoing relaxation. We investigate the phenomenological consequences of this evolution by numerically evolving linear scalar perturbations on prescribed, time-dependent Hayward-like geometries. We consider BHM--RBH--BHM histories in which an initially horizonless object temporarily develops a trapped region before returning to a horizonless configuration, through either a single bounce or a sequence of repeated bounces. Using horizon-penetrating Painlevé--Gullstrand coordinates, we follow the perturbations through the formation and disappearance of trapping horizons and compute the resulting waveforms and scalar-field energy. For histories with identical initial and final geometries, we find that changing the duration of the intermediate regular black hole phase produces differences in the amplitude and phase of the late-time signal, including its echoes. Longer trapped phases also yield greater energy amplification, consistent with the blueshift of outgoing modes near the inner trapping horizon. These results show that the late-time response of a dynamically relaxing BHM need not be determined by its final configuration alone: it can retain a memory of the dynamical history of its interior.

titles.title: Phenomenology of dynamical trapped regions

abstracts.value: Quantum modifications of black hole spacetimes can lead to observable departures from the predictions of classical general relativity, particularly in the strong-gravity regime near the event horizon. In this context, the coherent quantum black hole model introduces a sine-integral correction to the gravitational potential, characterized by a coherence scale Rs, which softens the central singularity and alters the near-horizon geometry. Motivated by the growing precision of black hole imaging and strong-field observations, we explore how these quantum-induced effects influence photon motion and the resulting shadow structure. Considering representative values within the interval Rs ∈ [0.5M, 1.2M], we show that the photon sphere shifts inward while the critical impact parameter decreases, reaching values such as bcrit ≈ 4.764M for <math altimg="si8.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>. Consequently, the shadow radius becomes systematically smaller and develops a more intricate structure than in the Schwarzschild case (<math altimg="si9.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></mrow><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mi>M</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>5.196</mn><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>). The analysis of the corresponding intensity distributions also reveals a pronounced enhancement of radiation near the shadow boundary, especially for intermediate coherence scales. This feature can be attributed to photons remaining longer within the modified near-horizon region before escaping toward distant observers. Such an increase in brightness may therefore provide a possible observational signature of quantum corrections at horizon scales. Furthermore, although the geometry allows radiation and energy to accumulate around an effective horizon surface, its response to perturbations differs from that expected for compact objects with stable light rings. Instead of contracting under backreaction effects, the accumulation surface shifts outward. These findings suggest that coherent quantum black holes preserve the asymptotic behavior of classical solutions at large distances while introducing potentially detectable imprints in strong-field gravitational lensing and black hole shadow observations.

Quantum modifications of black hole spacetimes can lead to observable departures from the predictions of classical general relativity, particularly in the strong-gravity regime near the event horizon. In this context, the coherent quantum black hole model introduces a sine-integral correction to the gravitational potential, characterized by a coherence scale \(R_s\), which softens the central singularity and alters the near-horizon geometry. Motivated by the growing precision of black hole imaging and strong-field observations, we explore how these quantum-induced effects influence photon motion and the resulting shadow structure. Considering representative values within the interval \(R_s \in [0.5M, 1.2M]\), we show that the photon sphere shifts inward while the critical impact parameter decreases, reaching values such as \(b_{\rm crit}\approx 4.764M\) for \(R_s=0.5M\). Consequently, the shadow radius becomes systematically smaller and develops a more intricate structure than in the Schwarzschild case (\(b_{\rm crit}=3\sqrt{3}M \approx 5.196M\)). The analysis of the corresponding intensity distributions also reveals a pronounced enhancement of radiation near the shadow boundary, especially for intermediate coherence scales. This feature can be attributed to photons remaining longer within the modified near-horizon region before escaping toward distant observers. Such an increase in brightness may therefore provide a possible observational signature of quantum corrections at horizon scales. Furthermore, although the geometry allows radiation and energy to accumulate around an effective horizon surface, its response to perturbations differs from that expected for compact objects with stable light rings. Instead of contracting under backreaction effects, the accumulation surface shifts outward.

titles.title: Shadow signatures and near-horizon energy accumulation in coherent quantum sine-integral black holes
Shadow signatures and near-horizon energy accumulation in coherent quantum sine-integral black holes

abstracts.value: We present a systematic analysis of spherically symmetric accretion flows onto thirteen non-rotating black hole spacetimes, including charged and regular black holes, scalar and dilaton fields, dark energy, cosmological constants, modified gravity, and parametrized metrics. We generalize the Michel solution to arbitrary diagonal spacetimes and investigate the density, temperature, velocity, Mach number, mass accretion rate, and bremsstrahlung luminosity equilibrium profiles. Using the Schwarzschild solution as a reference, we find significant deviations in the accretion flow, with cosmological-constant and dark-energy models strongly suppressing accretion, while regular and Yukawa-like spacetimes generally enhance it. We provide fitting formulas for the accretion rates and luminosities as functions of the spacetime parameters. We then explore two astrophysical applications: accretion onto supermassive black holes, such as Sgr A* and M87*, and the inferred progenitor masses of the intermediate-mass black holes associated with the GW190521 gravitational wave event. We find that observational uncertainties may allow us to probe signatures of deviations from the Schwarzschild spacetime.

titles.title: Relativistic Spherical Accretion in Nonrotating Black Hole Spacetimes: Astrophysical Implications

abstracts.value: In this article, we examine particle dynamics and Quasi-periodic oscillations within a charged Simpson-Visser-Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. We first analyze the behavior of the metric and black hole horizons under the competing impact of electric charge $Q$, regularization parameter $b$, and AdS radius $l$. The roots of the metric function reveal transitions between three distinct topological classes: non-extremal configurations featuring distinct inner and outer horizons, extremal limits with a single degenerate horizon, and strictly positive, horizonless wormhole geometries. By evaluating the effective potential, we determine how this modified geometry shifts the Innermost Stable Circular Orbit (ISCO) and alters the angular momentum and energy of test particles. Moreover, we derive the Keplerian, radial, and vertical frequencies to model quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs). We show that the interplay between the regularization parameter $b$ and the AdS radius $l$ significantly modifies twin-peak QPOs. In particular, $b$ drives fundamental QPO frequencies higher than those predicted by standard general relativistic backgrounds. Twin-peak high-frequency QPO data from two black-hole binaries disfavor the Schwarzschild limit at $\sim\!4σ$, but constrain only a degenerate combination of charge and AdS curvature, leaving the regularization parameter entirely unconstrained by the data.

titles.title: Charged Simpson-Visser-AdS spacetime: QPOs and observational constraints

abstracts.value: We analyze the radiative properties of a general class of static and spherically symmetric black holes described by three independent shape functions, that encompass a broad family of regular and quantum-corrected geometries. We consider a minimally coupled massless scalar field, and derive the Hawking temperature and graybody factor for the different geometries. While the Hawking temperature is determined by the near-horizon geometry, the graybody factor depends on the scattering properties of the entire exterior spacetime, and therefore exhibits a richer dependence on the deformation parameters, frequency, and angular mode. Then we particularize to geometries that describe slight deformations of the Schwarzschild black hole, and obtain analytic expressions for the leading corrections to the graybody factor. Finally, we apply our results to several specific well-known black-hole models, including Reissner-Nordström, Bardeen, Hayward, Simpson-Visser, as well as geometries inspired by loop quantum gravity. In general, the deformations lead to colder horizons than Schwarzschild, and their effect on the graybody factor is frequency-dependent: the transmission of low-frequency modes is suppressed, whereas it is enhanced for high-frequency modes. This behavior is found for all but one of the geometries considered, which exhibits just the opposite trend. The analyzed modifications to the Hawking spectrum may therefore have relevant observational consequences, potentially providing signatures of deviations from the Schwarzschild geometry.

titles.title: Hawking radiation and graybody factor of slightly deformed Schwarzschild black holes

abstracts.value: Regular black holes avoid the central singularity by replacing it with a de Sitter core. We ask what cosmology follows if the same idea is brought to the early universe. Regular metrics define a position-dependent cosmological term, $Λ_{\rm eff}(r)=8πG ρ_{\rm MS}(r)$, and there is no unique way to carry it over to the expanding universe. We follow three different prescriptions: a Newtonian one following McCrea and Milne, a running vacuum evaluated at Hubble radius and a quasi-local one based on Misner-Sharp mass. We apply each of them to six regular black hole metrics and explore their consequences. In the Newtonian case the Friedmann equations are solved in closed form for the Hayward metric, and in terms of standard special functions or numerically for the others, and describe a universe that starts in a de Sitter phase and ends as dust (i.e. an inflationary model instead of dark energy). We find that in all three prescriptions a monotonically decreasing core density gives an equation of state that never crosses $w=-1$, and thus the phantom behaviour suggested by DESI would require a density shell which a regular core does not have. The three prescriptions agree on the de Sitter core but differ at late times, and we quantify the difference against the DESI DR2 results. We also point out that a single regularisation length cannot serve as both the inflationary and the dark-energy scale.

titles.title: Regular Cosmologies: Three Distinct Routes

abstracts.value: A recently proposed class of black-bounce solutions sourced by anisotropic fluids, whose exterior reproduces the Reissner-Nordström geometry all the way down to a minimal-area bounce, was put forward by Lessa and Olmo. In this work, we show that this solution conceals a thin-shell structure precisely at the bounce. Motivated by this observation, we construct a new class of black-bounce solutions with static, spherical symmetry featuring the emergence of a minimal-area bounce supported by a thin shell. This nontrivial topological structure is shown to arise from the degeneracy of the metric at the bounce, where the inverse metric becomes ill-defined, leading to curvature tensors with distributional discontinuities precisely at that point. As a consequence, a delta-function thin shell of energy-condition-violating matter is necessarily present at the bounce. To generate such solutions, we draw on proposals from quantum gravity that predict the existence of a fundamental minimum length scale, employing energy density profiles that encode these quantum-gravitational effects in an effective manner, replacing the point-like description of matter at minimal-length scales with a smeared one. We consider two well-motivated profiles, of Lorentzian and Gaussian type, to generate a novel class of solutions exhibiting the features of either regular black holes or wormholes, whose center conceals a thin-shell bounce. In addition, we investigate the thermodynamics of these compact objects.

titles.title: Thin-Shell Black Bounce

abstracts.value: Strong gravitational lensing is one of our most direct probes of gravity in the strong-field regime, and horizonless ultracompact objects are expected to leave lensing signatures that are qualitatively different from those of black holes. Recent EHT observations of supermassive compact objects have opened new avenues for testing gravity in the strong-field regime. These observations do not rule out the possibility that some compact objects may be horizonless rather than black holes and may produce distinct gravitational lensing signatures. In this work, we study strong gravitational lensing by rotating black-bounce spacetimes, regular geometries that smoothly interpolate between black holes and traversable wormholes. We analyse two models that extend the Simpson-Visser spacetime, each with a distinct mass function that affects the near-throat structure. We find that horizonless spacetimes can support both an outer unstable photon sphere and an inner stable photon sphere. Images associated with trajectories passing inside the outer photon sphere show larger angular separations and magnifications than those formed outside, in some cases by several orders of magnitude, which may be relevant for future high-resolution observations such as ng-EHT. When we compare with EHT observations of Sgr A*, both the black hole and the horizonless compact object remain consistent when the spin is low. At the same time, differences become more apparent at higher spins within the parameter space considered. We also prove that black-bounce spacetimes can admit closed photon ring structures, in contrast to Kerr naked singularities, which produce an open arc. Altogether, this work is the first analytic study of strong gravitational lensing in rotating horizonless black-bounce spacetimes and provides a framework applicable to other similar compact objects.

titles.title: Analytical treatment of strong gravitational lensing by rotating black-bounce spacetimes with and without horizons

abstracts.value: The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, proportional to one quarter of the horizon area, is fundamental in black hole thermodynamics and can also be understood via the AdS/CFT correspondence, such as the 3D BTZ black hole and 2D CFT. In this work, we adopt the Kerr/CFT approach to analyze the central charge and black hole entropy for regular extremal black-bounce spacetimes, including the counterparts of the Kerr, Kerr-Newman, and Reissner-Nordström black holes. These spacetimes are free of curvature singularities at $r=0$. We derive the near horizon geometries of these spacetimes and find that they exhibit enhanced symmetry, namely SL$(2,\mathbb{R})\times \mathrm{U}(1)$ or SL$(2,\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{SO}(3)$. By imposing appropriate boundary conditions, we analyze their asymptotic symmetry groups, which contain diffeomorphisms as well as the $\mathrm{U}(1)_{\rm gauge}$ symmetry arising from the electromagnetic field. We then extract the central charge from the charge algebra and evaluate the left-moving temperature of the Frolov-Thorne vacuum. It is worth emphasizing that in the black-bounce Kerr-Newman case, the central charge from the electromagnetic contribution vanishes. Furthermore, in the black-bounce Reissner-Nordström case, we uplift the 4D geometry to a 5D configuration by incorporating a $\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge fiber. Our results show that the microscopic entropy calculated from the Cardy formula is consistent with the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. This agreement suggests that the Kerr/CFT approach remains valid for certain regular spacetimes without curvature singularities, thereby providing a microscopic statistical understanding of black hole entropy.

titles.title: Central charge and black hole entropy for regular extremal black-bounce spacetimes

abstracts.value: In this paper, we investigate the chaos bound through the local radial instability of charged spinning test particles on unstable circular orbits in the black-bounce--Kerr--Newman spacetime. Our results show that violation of the bound is governed by the competition between the local orbital-instability scale and the surface gravity scale, with variations of the black hole background and the particle dynamics providing two complementary routes to the same threshold crossing. Background variations affect both scales and can drive the system into the bound-violating regime when the surface gravity is suppressed more strongly than the orbital instability. At fixed background, by contrast, the surface gravity remains unchanged, and the transition across the threshold is driven by changes in the unstable orbit dynamics induced by the particle parameters. The background-controlled and probe-dynamics-controlled routes therefore represent two realizations of a unified horizon--orbit scale competition rather than independent mechanisms.

titles.title: Horizon--orbit scale competition underlying chaos bound violation for spinning particles
Horizon--orbit scale competition in chaos bound violation for spinning particles in the black-bounce--Kerr--Newman spacetime

abstracts.value: A dark matter density profile alone does not determine the spacetime around a black hole; the radial stress must be prescribed separately and governs the strong-field orbital response. We study a Bardeen black hole in a Hernquist halo through three spherical models sharing the same density, mass function, and cutoff but differing in radial stress: a halo with $p_r^{\mathrm{DM}}=-ρ_{\mathrm{DM}}$, its truncated form, and a truncated Einstein cluster with $p_r^{\mathrm{DM}}=0$. Treating the halo as a small perturbation, we derive a first-order criterion for the leading innermost stable circular orbit shift, $C_λ=C_ρ+λC_p$. The two truncated closures shift this orbit in opposite directions for the Hernquist profile, and unexpanded calculations for five density profiles confirm the predicted signs. Checks using a Hayward background and a published Dehnen-halo result show that the criterion is not restricted to the Bardeen-Hernquist system. A continuous stress interpolation identifies a critical closure at which the leading shift vanishes. For a representative four-year extreme-mass-ratio inspiral, changing the radial stress at fixed density and cutoff produces a phase difference of several radians in a leading-order adiabatic treatment.

titles.title: Radial Stress and the Innermost Stable Circular Orbit of a Bardeen Black Hole in a Dark Matter Halo: A First-Order Response Criterion

abstracts.value: We present a critical analysis of electromagnetic (EM) field configurations in exponentially modified Schwarzschild-like black hole (BH) spacetimes, correcting fundamental inconsistencies in the solution recently proposed in Ref. [1]. The exponentially modified metric <math altimg="si13.svg"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>M</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">/</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.16em"/><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> represents a regular BH solution eliminating central singularities. However, Ref. [1] employs power-law approximations <math altimg="si14.svg"><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>C</mi><mspace width="0.16em"/><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> for the vector potential radial function, neglecting exponential corrections that propagate through Maxwell’s equations. This constitutes a critical mathematical error: proper substitution of the exponential metric into EM field equations yields differential equations inheriting exponential terms that cannot be eliminated without destroying consistency. We rigorously demonstrate that power-law approximations introduce relative errors exceeding <math altimg="si15.svg"><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></math> in strong-field regimes near r ∼ 3M, invalidating EM descriptions and conclusions regarding quasinormal modes (QNMs) and energy extraction presented in Ref. [1]. To provide the correct treatment, we develop a perturbative expansion in a/r ≪ 1, deriving exact zeroth-order solutions containing essential logarithmic terms <math altimg="si16.svg"><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> and first-order corrections exhibiting divergent near-horizon behavior with persistent large-radius modifications. Imposing regularity constraints at asymptotic infinity and the event horizon (EH) reveals an eigenvalue problem: only discrete parameter families (M, a, B0) admit physically acceptable configurations, predicting quantized magnetic field states absent in standard Schwarzschild geometry and providing observationally testable signatures distinguishing modified from classical BH physics. We further show that the magnetic interaction enters the QNM effective potential through the same radial function φ(r), so the corrected configuration shifts the long-lived, quasi-resonant spectrum reported for this background and calls for its quantitative revision.

titles.title: Revisiting magnetic field configuration in Schwarzschild-like black hole

abstracts.value: We develop a general framework for constructing massive black bounce geometries from massless wormhole seeds by introducing a position-dependent mass function while preserving the underlying areal-radius profile. We apply this procedure to the generalized Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole and obtain a new family of generalized Bardeen-like black bounce space-times, which continuously interpolates between traversable wormholes and regular black holes. We investigate the motion of massive particles and photons and show that, in contrast with the simpler orbital structure of the massless generalized Ellis-Bronnikov geometry, the generalized Bardeen-like space-time can exhibit multiple circular orbits and a rich light ring structure, including configurations with two unstable circular photon orbits separated by a stable one. We determine the corresponding photon sphere and shadow radii and compare our predictions with Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*, deriving observational constraints on the parameter space of the model. We further investigate the optical appearance produced by a geometrically and optically thin accretion disk through ray tracing. Multiple light rings generate characteristic nested structures in the high-resolution intensity profiles, whose relative brightness is strongly affected by the mass deformation and gravitational redshift. However, after modeling the finite angular resolution of the EHT with a Gaussian beam convolution, these fine structures are largely washed out, revealing a strong observational degeneracy between these exotic compact objects and standard black hole geometries at current EHT resolution.

titles.title: From massless wormholes to massive black bounces: Shadows and multiple light rings
From massless wormholes to massive black bounces: Relativistic astrophysical observations of shadows and multiple light rings

abstracts.value: In this work, we derive phenomenological constraints on a symmetric black-bounce geometry supported by an anisotropic fluid. We investigate the effects of the bounce parameter and the matter parameter on classical and strong-field observables, considering the perihelion advance, light deflection, Shapiro time delay, and black-hole shadow. In the weak-field regime, we obtain analytical corrections to the corresponding general-relativistic predictions and use Solar-System measurements to constrain the parameter space. We find that the matter parameter is generally constrained more strongly than the minimum-radius scale, reflecting the suppressed dependence of weak-field observables on the bounce parameter. In the strong-field regime, we show that the asymptotic shadow radius depends directly on the matter parameter, whereas the bounce parameter enters through the existence condition of the outer unstable photon orbit rather than through an independent correction to the shadow size. These results highlight the distinct roles played by the matter and bounce parameters in weak- and strong-field observables and provide complementary constraints on the parameter space of the symmetric black-bounce geometry.

titles.title: Bounds on Black Bounces from Phenomenological Imprints

abstracts.value: In this manuscript, we investigate the shadow and polarization images of a Simpson-Visser rotating black hole surrounded by a ballistic approximation accretion flow model. Solving the numerically geodesic and radiative transfer equations, we discuss the influence of the regularization parameter $g$, spin parameter $a$, and observer inclination angle $θ_o$ on the resulting images at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$ with an infalling motion. The results interpret that, a bright circular ring corresponding to higher-order images is observed, accompanied by an inner region of decreased intensity. Both $g$ and $a$ has little influence on the size of the higher-order images, but significantly changes their shape and intensity distribution. Whereas, variation in $θ_o$ modify the image morphology, producing a crescent-shaped bright region on the left side. Finally, the polarization patterns trace the brightness distribution and vary with both $g$ and $a$, reflecting the spacetime structure. These results demonstrates that the intensity and polarization in thick disk models provide probes of Simpson-Visser rotating black holes and near-horizon accretion physics.

titles.title: Shadows and Polarimetric Signatures of Rotating Simpson-Visser Black Holes with Thick Disk Illumination

abstracts.value: We construct the first-law-consistent entropy of a geometrically minimal-length-deformed Schwarzschild spacetime, obtained via the areal-radius substitution $R(r)=\sqrt{r^{2}+\ell^{2}}$ on $r\in[0,+\infty)$ with $f(R)=1-2M/R$, whose nonvanishing Einstein tensor sources an effective geometric fluid with no classical matter counterpart. Integrating the first law gives $S=π[r_{h}R_{h}+\ell^{2}\ln((r_{h}+R_{h})/\ell)]$. This coincides in functional form with the semiclassical term found independently by Joshi and Joshi, but we fix its boundary condition $S(r_h=0)=0$ on independent physical grounds and adopt it, rather than the Bekenstein--Hawking area law, as the complete entropy of the model, building the free energy, geometrothermodynamics, and mode-stability analysis on it. Evaporation, governed by the Helmholtz free energy $F(M)$, terminates at $M_{\min}=\ell/2$ in a previously unrecognised endpoint: a degenerate extremal regular black hole, where the regular centre coincides with a degenerate Killing horizon of quadratic order, $f\approx r^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$, at areal radius $\ell$, with $T_{H}\to 0$, $S\to 0$, $C\to 0^{+}$, and finite curvature everywhere; we display its Penrose--Carter structure for the first time. The same entropy, with $\ell$, defines the equilibrium state space of a Legendre-invariant geometrothermodynamic (GTD) description whose curvature scalar diverges independently at the Davies-type transition $M^{*}=\ell/\sqrt{2}$ and at $M_{\min}$, a divergence with no counterpart in the minimal-length black hole literature, specific to a genuine horizon at $S=0$. We embed this remnant within the observational discriminant noted qualitatively by Tsukamoto: exact shadow degeneracy combined with a measurable photon-ring flux enhancement $r_{n}=e^{-2π/a}>e^{-2π}$, accessible to next-generation very-long-baseline interferometry.

titles.title: First-Law Entropy and a Degenerate Extremal Remnant in a Minimal-Length Simpson--Visser-Type Regular Black Hole: Geometrothermodynamics, Phase Structure, and Observational Discriminants

abstracts.value: The Event Horizon Telescope images of M87* and Sgr A* give us a unique chance to test gravity in the strong field regime and assess deviations from the Kerr solution. We study the shadows of rotating nonsingular black holes—namely, generalized Ghosh black holes (GGBHs), given by the mass function <math altimg="si52.svg"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>M</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, which reduces to the Kerr black hole (k → 0) and to the original Ghosh model (<math altimg="si13.svg"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>). We calculate the photon’s trajectory via the Hamilton-Jacobi method and construct the shadow seen by a distant observer. For a high spin <math altimg="si53.svg"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow></math>, increasing k/M from 0 to 0.5 reduces the shadow size by about 13% and the shadow area by about 24%, while making the shape more distorted (up to  ∼ 20%). For larger values k/M ∼ 1.0, the area can decrease by nearly 30%. However, increasing n reduces these effects, and for n ≥ 3 the shadow becomes very close to the Kerr case (differences below  ∼ 5%). To compare with observations, we use two simple shadow quantities: the area A and the oblateness D. Using EHT observational data, we find that for M87* (17<sup loc="post">∘</sup> inclination, 37.8μas diameter), the parameter is constrained as k/M ≲ 0.133 for <math altimg="si13.svg"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. For Sgr A* (50<sup loc="post">∘</sup> inclination, 48.7μas diameter), the bound is k/M ≲ 0.09162 when a/M is near the Schwarzschild limit, while the overall allowed range extends to k/M ≲ 0.449 when considering the full parameter space and the 41.7μas constraint. These limits become weaker for larger n. Overall, the GGBH model is consistent with current EHT observations and provides a viable framework for testing deviations from the Kerr geometry. Future observations with improved resolution may help to detect or further constrain such deviations.

titles.title: Parameter estimation of generalized Ghosh black holes using shadow observables and event horizon telescope constraints
